title: Born weights are Fubini-Study volumes
abstract: A machine-checked proof that Born weights are Fubini-Study volumes. For a ray [z] of C^(M+1), a pure state measured in the standard basis, its Born probability vector is (|<e_0, z>|^2, ..., |<e_M, z>|^2) / |z|^2, a point of the probability simplex (also the moment map of the torus action on CP^M). Let mu be any probability measure on CP^M invariant under every unitary; there is exactly one, the Fubini-Study measure. The identity is proved as two volume identities and a frequency corollary. First (born_vector_uniform_of_invariant): for a pure state chosen with law mu, the Born probability vector is uniformly distributed on the simplex, so the Fubini-Study measure of the states whose Born vector lies in a region R is M! times the Lebesgue measure of R in free coordinates. Second, for a given state (born_weight_eq_measure_cell, born_weight_eq_measure_apexCell): for a unit vector psi, cone the simplex from the Born vector of psi; the states whose Born vector lies in the cell opposite vertex i have mu-measure |<e_i, psi>|^2, the Born weight of outcome i. This holds for every unit psi, including those with vanishing coordinates, and the cells depend on psi. Third (born_frequencies_tendsto_born_weights): invariant sampling reproduces the Born weights as long-run frequencies; for pure states drawn pairwise independently with law mu, almost surely the fraction of draws in the cell opposite vertex i tends to |<e_i, psi>|^2, by the strong law of large numbers. The theorems show that Born weights are Fubini-Study volumes; they do not derive the Born rule or say why measurement outcomes follow it. The first form is classical: Archimedes' hat-box theorem for M = 1 and in general the Duistermaat-Heckman pushforward for the torus action on CP^M. The proof does not use the Duistermaat-Heckman theorem; it goes through Gaussians, proves the first form, and derives the second and third from it. The second and third are elementary corollaries of the first; no source stating them in this form was located. No priority or novelty is claimed.
